text: You write one line of SQL. Insert into orders. And hit run.
But under the hood, your database runs five jobs before that OK comes back.
Job one. The connection pool hands your query to a free worker.
Job two. The parser validates your SQL, and the planner picks the cheapest path.
Job three, the critical one. Postgres appends the change to the write-ahead log, and fsyncs it to disk.
Only after the log is durable does the row land in the buffer pool.
Job four. At checkpoint, dirty pages finally flush to your table files.
Why the log first? One sequential write beats random writes everywhere. That is how one line of SQL becomes a durable commit.
